The most common win left on "Casino 7s" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $1,000, and 29 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If you play "Casino 7s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

2776.headline: Prize table details

2779.body:
"Gnome for the Holidays" has 52 of 57 top prizes left and is still new. Only a small slice of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

The numbers for "Gnome for the Holidays" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2779.headline: How much has sold

2780.body:
"Holiday Countdown" just went on sale in Texas. The game has ten full prize levels with five top prizes of $100,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

If you play "Holiday Countdown" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2780.headline: A new game is here

2781.body:
"The Perfect Gift" just reached Texas stores with five top prizes of $250,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

Every line of The Perfect Gift's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2781.headline: A new game is here

2782.body:
"$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" has joined the Texas lineup at $20 with four top prizes of $1 million. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Everything above about "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" comes from the Texas Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
